title: Quarrel with Martel, marriage to Hillary, and hired by Doc Moon
summary: After a falling out with Old Man Martel, whose daughter Hillary he married, Joe borrowed an alto sax in Opelousas, auditioned and was hired at twenty-one dollars a week.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Well, yeah, of course! That's what I'm coming to. He didn't travel across the nation, but we went as far as Ohio and Illinois. We went through Arkansas when we left Louisiana. Anyway, it was a bootlegging joint. It was Prohibition, and I was in there getting a drink... I was working in the Martel Band, but I had quit the Martel Band and was working in the shoe shop. I had a falling out with Old Man Martel. In fact, to tell you the truth, I married his daughter.

Yeah. Her name was Hillary. And Old Man Martel wanted me to quit drinking and quit the shoe shop job, and just concentrate on music and stay home. I said, "I ain't gonna do no such thing. I'll work in the shoe shop as long as I want." I needed that extra money. At that time I think we was workin' only two nights a week, because work was falling off for some reason. Anyway, we separated. I wasn't playing with him.

And I was in this little old bootlegging joint there in Opelousas, and this Big Boy, this guitar and banjo player, we got to talking. And I says, "You guys ever use...?" "Oh yeah." I was rooming in a house where a guy had a saxophone, an alto saxophone. And I had borrowed it from him. I can't think of his name... Anyway, I asked him to loan it to me, because Big Boy... They was playin' a week in this... I told him I was a musician and I played saxophone, and he says, "I'll tell you, Doc Moon really wants a saxophone player; he's been trying to get one." I says, "Well, he's got it. He's got that Cliff that plays clarinet." He said, "Well, Cliff can't play no saxophone." And he says, "If you bring your saxophone, Doc Moon probably would hire you."

So anyway, that night at the medicine show, I brought it and played. Got up there and did something, one of them little old simple tunes, like "Margie" and things like that. So Doc Moon says, "Yeah." In fact...

...in the shop there. So he said, "Yeah, I could use you on the saxophone, and pay you twenty-one dollars a week." I said, "Well, the only thing is, I don't have a saxophone." He said, "That saxophone don't belong to you?" I said, "I had to borrow this thing from..." The guy was named Leonard something; he was trying to learn. And Doc Moon said, "Well, if that's all it takes, when we get to Lafayette, I'll buy you a saxophone, and then you can pay me back." Lafayette, Louisiana was only maybe fifteen miles from Opelousas.
So we go to Lafayette, to this music store, and buy this alto saxophone. They had one in there, a Conn, nickel-plated alto saxophone -- it cost ninety-nine dollars.
